page: Amazon Web Services c6g.large is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARMv8 architecture, it features 2 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 model running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, with no local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. Network connectivity is delivered via a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps under the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate a moderate single-core capability alongside lower multi-core and memory throughput. The stress-ng single-core CPU test registers at 1519.49, placing it in the average tier, whereas the multi-core stress-ng result of 3010.97 falls into the lower 25th percentile. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show 117.37 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 38.93 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX or AMX, but supports hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

From a resource density perspective, the c6g.large offers a cost-efficient entry point for ARM-native workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without the overhead of hyperthreading. Due to its memory capacity of 4.0 GB and baseline network speed, it is best suited for lightweight compute-focused tasks, basic web serving, single-threaded application testing, and software compilation pipelines optimized for the arm64 architecture.
